artifact.title: Research plan and instruments
artifact.question: How did we learn how engagement teams work, with what methods, what rigor and what limits?
artifact.iDecided: the method mix, the sampling frame per method and contextual inquiry as the anchor.
artifact.weBuilt: the instruments, the recruiting screeners and the SME session series. Fieldwork and coding were team work. Design team of three at this phase.

rqs.text: How do engagement teams gather, test and review evidence during busy season? Where does the time go?
What makes a workpaper hard to review, and what does a reviewer look for first?
What would each role hand to an agent, what would they never hand off and what would make them trust it?
Where in the lifecycle do errors and rework originate?
What baseline do we measure change against?

methods.name: Contextual inquiry, full fieldwork days
methods.label: planned target
methods.analysis: Field notes coded to the codebook (03). Pain points placed on the nine lifecycle stages.
methods.limits: Observer effect. Access limited to teams that consent during busy season. Six teams cannot represent every territory.

methods.name: Semi-structured interviews
methods.label: planned target
methods.analysis: Transcripts coded; themes rated by an ordinal evidence rubric, never by count.
methods.limits: Self-report and recall. Role-specific probes risk leading if the interviewer drifts.

methods.name: Diary study, two weeks in busy season
methods.label: planned target
methods.analysis: Entries coded by lifecycle stage and rework cause.
methods.limits: Attrition under deadline pressure. Entries skew to memorable events.

methods.name: SME sessions with methodology reviewers
methods.label: planned target
methods.analysis: Decisions captured to decisions.md; taxonomy and checkpoint rules to 08.
methods.limits: Methodology view, not field view. Sessions validate rules; they do not observe behavior.

methods.name: Time-and-motion study of evidence review
methods.label: planned target
methods.analysis: Descriptive statistics of step durations. Where time goes by step.
methods.limits: Small n. One observer. Step boundaries are a judgment.

methods.name: Workpaper rework audit
methods.label: planned target
methods.analysis: Rework causes by audit area and lifecycle stage. Double-coded subset with agreement check.
methods.limits: Prior engagements only. Review notes record what reviewers wrote, not what they thought.

methods.name: Baseline survey, SUS and tool satisfaction
methods.label: planned target
methods.analysis: SUS scored by the standard formula. Satisfaction descriptives by role.
methods.limits: Response bias toward the dissatisfied. SUS is a blunt instrument for a tool set rather than one tool.

methods.name: Pilot telemetry
methods.label: planned target
methods.analysis: Task completion, time to conclusion, approval and edit rates, review latency. Descriptives only.
methods.limits: Pilot users are early adopters. Events measure the product, not the audit.

methods.name: Usability round 1, moderated think-aloud
methods.label: planned target
methods.analysis: Findings table with severity on the shared 1 to 4 scale.

methods.name: Dry run with engagement teams
methods.label: real
methods.analysis: Intake taxonomy, triage 2x2, themes. Repository becomes the regression bench.
methods.limits: Voluntary reporting. Team self-selection. Recency bias.

methods.name: Usability round 2, task-based with metrics
methods.label: planned target
methods.analysis: Task success, time on task, errors, trust calibration.
methods.limits: Lab tasks are cleaner than fieldwork.

methods.name: Card sort and tree test
methods.label: planned target
methods.analysis: Agreement matrix, tree test success and directness.
methods.limits: Tests labels and structure, not use.

methods.name: Usability round 3, unmoderated with SUS
methods.label: planned target
methods.analysis: SUS trend against the M7 baseline.
